summary: Rewrote classify.sh heartbeat logic. Removed FIRST_MSG_MARKER block and blanket heartbeat line. Added flag-based system: /tmp/orch-ready-$SID JSON flag written on every message when ready tasks exist (or refreshed if >10min old). Flag-derived context injected into CTX with loop_control start instructions, fallback ScheduleWakeup, and loop-active wakeup. All classify/routing/model/gate logic preserved unchanged.

subject: Update classify.sh: smart ready-task flag, context injection with labels, wakeup timing
description:
Rewrite the orchestrator heartbeat logic in classify.sh:

1. EVERY message (not just first): check if flag /tmp/orch-ready-$SID exists. If no flag, query daemon for ready tasks. If ready tasks found, write flag file containing task labels + timestamp (JSON). If flag exists, recheck only if >10 min since last check (update timestamp).

2. ScheduleWakeup instruction: only inject when flag exists. Inject ready task labels so agent can judge priority. Format: "[Orchestrator] N tasks ready: [label1, label2, ...]. If user has higher-priority work, ignore. Otherwise call loop_control(start) to pick them up. Use ScheduleWakeup: 7200s if idle (auto-accept on wakeup if still no user activity), 270s if loop active, 1200s if nothing."

3. Auto-accept logic in wakeup prompt: if woken after 2hr idle (no user messages since flag set), call loop_control(start) automatically. Check /active-claim?session=SID — if session has active claim, skip dispatch.

4. Remove the current blanket "Call ScheduleWakeup every 30 seconds" instruction — replace with the conditional flag-based injection above.

5. Flag cleared when: user explicitly declines, or loop_control(start) is called (tasks dispatched).

Read classify.sh carefully before editing. Preserve all existing routing/model/gate logic.
